$comment: The Phase 2 boundary review. Every B, X and D posture in artifacts/prompts/ai-standards-spec.md is recorded here with the adjacent-pack standard it defers to or crosswalks, read at the recorded commit. Read `evidence[].observation` as OBSERVED: it is a scope or rule statement quoted or paraphrased from a file on disk. Read `verdict` and `reasoning` as INFERRED: they are this review's judgment about what the observation implies.
$signOffNote: No human has signed this review off. The evidence below was collected by reading the named files; the judgment in each `verdict` is not a human boundary decision and must not be recorded as one. Standard 7 R1 states that whether this pack genuinely defers rather than restates is a judgment about the meaning of two documents, and no check makes it.
method: For each non-O posture, the named adjacent pack's standard was opened at the recorded commit and its Scope section read, together with the rule ids in its catalog. A posture is CONFIRMED when the named standard's scope covers the concern; NARROWED when it covers only part of it and the remainder is this pack's outright; CHANGED when the evidence does not support the plan's posture at all.

excludedAuthorities.reason: Frozen. Its own FROZEN.md states it 'is not the portfolio's standards authority, and must not be adopted as one'.
excludedAuthorities.observation: FROZEN.md present at F:/Repos/StandardsOrchestrator/FROZEN.md and read on 2026-09-04.

postures.title: Autonomy Levels and Delegated Authority

evidence.observation: Scope: 'Applies to any project exposing capabilities to AI agents'. The rule is level required, validationType manual-review, nonExemptible false.

postures.reasoning: ES governs whether a capability surface separates recommendation from application. It does not define autonomy levels or the authority delegated at each. AIStandards is canonical for the levels; the ES rule is precedent for the separation they rest on.

postures.title: Context and Corpus Provenance
postures.owner: MachineLearningStandards for training data; AIStandards for retrieval corpora, prompt fixtures and eval sets

evidence.observation: Scope: 'Applies to every dataset used to train, validate, evaluate, or calibrate a model, including datasets assembled by joining or filtering others.'
Scope: 'Applies to any dataset whose contents can change over time'.

postures.reasoning: A retrieval corpus consulted at inference time by a hosted model is not a dataset used to train, validate, evaluate or calibrate a model, so ML 3 does not reach it. The deference is genuine for training data and the baseline carve-out is genuine for retrieval.

postures.title: Evaluation Plans for Generative Systems
postures.owner: MachineLearningStandards for metric selection and comparison; AIStandards for generative framing

evidence.observation: Scope: 'Applies to every evaluation of a model, and to every claim about model quality made outside the project.'
Scope: 'Applies to every reported evaluation figure that will be compared to another'.

postures.reasoning: ML 12's scope is broad enough to cover generative evaluation where a metric is reported. What it does not cover is rubric and judge-model design, and non-numeric output where there is no figure to select a metric for. AIStandards adds only that.
unknowns: Whether ML's maintainers read 'every evaluation of a model' as including a hosted model the project did not train. The wording admits both readings and nothing in ML resolves it.

postures.title: Benchmark Integrity and Contamination
postures.owner: MachineLearningStandards for train/test leakage; AIStandards outright for pretraining contamination

evidence.observation: Scope: 'Applies to every path by which information unavailable at prediction time can reach a model during' [training].

postures.reasoning: ML 8 governs leakage introduced by the project's own pipeline. Contamination of a third-party pretrained model by a public benchmark predates the project entirely, involves no pipeline the project controls, and is outside ML 8's stated path. The plan's B posture assumed ML covered the whole concern; it covers one half. The other half is AIStandards' outright and must say so rather than defer into a gap.
unknowns: Pretraining contamination is not detectable from a repository at all. The AIStandards half is expected to be manual-review or not-evaluable; which is a Phase 3 decision.

postures.title: Uncertainty Expression and Abstention
postures.owner: PredictionStandards for systems emitting prediction records; AIStandards otherwise; UIUXDesignStandards for how it is conveyed in an interface

evidence.observation: Scope: 'Applies to every prediction. Abstentions are outside it'. The rules 'declare appliesTo: prediction and the evaluator reports them not-applicable on an abstention record'.
Scope: 'Applies to every record and to the systems that produce them.'
R6: 'Where a system has a defensible measure of its own confidence, the interface SHOULD convey it. An interface MUST NOT invent a confidence indication that the underlying system does not produce.'

postures.reasoning: The plan's D posture would have deferred this item to PredictionStandards outright. The evidence does not support it: PredictionStandards' rules are scoped to prediction records and report not-applicable in their absence, so an assistant that hedges in prose and emits no record would be governed by nobody. Deferring into that gap is the silent-drop failure this review exists to catch. AIStandards states the general requirement and defers to PredictionStandards for any system that does emit prediction records.
unknowns: Whether a generative system's self-reported confidence is a 'defensible measure' at all. This is a model-behaviour question, so the AIStandards rule is expected to be not-evaluable.

postures.title: Citation and Source Attribution
postures.owner: AIStandards for whether a citation is owed and whether it resolves; UIUXDesignStandards for how sources are presented

evidence.observation: R7: 'Where output cites or draws on sources, those sources SHOULD be reachable. A citation the user cannot open is a claim, not evidence.'

postures.reasoning: The plan marked this owned outright. UIUX 26 R7 already governs the presentation half. Keeping O would mean two packs asserting requirements about citation presentation with no recorded division, which is exactly the condition Standard 7 exists to prevent.

postures.title: Grounding and Hallucination Control

evidence.observation: Description: 'No API, library capability, configuration option, or repository fact is asserted without having been checked.' The subject is the engineering agent's claims about a codebase.
R1: 'Where a user could reasonably take generated output for verified, human-authored fact, the interface MUST mark it.'

postures.reasoning: The plan crosswalked this to ai.no-fabricated-capabilities. The evidence does not support it: that rule's subject is an agent inventing APIs and repository facts, not a deployed system generating ungrounded output for a user. Recording it as precedent would assert a correspondence that does not hold, and a false crosswalk is worse than none because it implies a division of ownership nobody made. The nearest real neighbour is UIUX ai-ux.no-generated-as-verified, which governs presentation and is recorded as an adjacency rather than a crosswalk.

postures.title: Capability Honesty to Users

evidence.observation: level forbidden, severity error, nonExemptible true, validationType manual-review, assurance none. $assuranceNote: 'Detecting a fabricated API means resolving every symbol against every dependency's real surface - a type checker's job, and one this framework does not do.'
R8: 'Language implying memory, intent, understanding, or agency the system does not have misleads users about what it will do. Personality is permitted; misrepresentation is not.'

postures.reasoning: ES 53's rule is genuine precedent for the prohibition on claiming a capability nobody checked. AIStandards is canonical because its subject is what a deployed AI system tells its users, not what an engineering agent tells a reviewer. UIUX 26 R8 is added as a second precedent the plan did not record.

postures.title: Model and Prompt Lineage
postures.owner: MachineLearningStandards for feature and dataset lineage; AIStandards outright for prompt lineage

evidence.observation: Scope: 'Applies to every feature supplied to a model, including features that appear to be raw columns'.
Scope: 'Applies to any dataset whose contents can change over time'.

postures.reasoning: A prompt is not a feature supplied to a model in ML 17's sense — it is the instruction, not a column derived from upstream data — so ML 17 does not reach prompt lineage at all. The dataset half defers genuinely to ML 4. The plan's undifferentiated B would have deferred prompt lineage to a standard that does not cover it.

postures.title: Reproducibility Under Nondeterminism

evidence.observation: Scope: 'Applies to every experiment whose result is reported, compared against, or used to justify a decision'.
Scope: 'Applies to every source of randomness that affects a reported result.' The standard 'requires the seed, and requires equally that the seed not be treated as a guarantee it cannot give.'

postures.reasoning: The strongest deference in the catalog. ML 15 and 16 own training reproducibility outright. AIStandards adds only nondeterminism originating at a remote inference endpoint, which no seed the project controls can remove — a case ML 16 explicitly acknowledges is outside what a seed guarantees. This item must stay the shortest in the catalog.

postures.title: AI Observability
postures.owner: MachineLearningStandards for deployed-model monitoring; EngineeringStandards for silenced failures; AIStandards for inference-call tracing

evidence.observation: Scope: 'Applies to every deployed model from the moment it serves its first prediction'.
Scope: 'Applies to every model serving predictions that influence a decision, from the point of deployment onward.'
EngineeringStandards uses the `observability.` segment, which AIStandards also reserves. No full id collides; see sharedSegments.

postures.reasoning: A project calling a hosted model deploys no model of its own, so ML 21 and 24 do not reach it. AIStandards owns inference-call tracing for that case and defers wherever the project serves a model. The EngineeringStandards adjacency is a shared-segment finding the plan did not record.

postures.title: Accessibility of AI Features

evidence.observation: Nineteen accessibility rules in the UIUXDesignStandards catalog, across three dedicated standards.

postures.reasoning: The strongest D in the catalog. AIStandards MUST NOT mint an accessibility rule; the item exists to record the obligation and name the owner, which is what departure 3 of the tokenisation requires.

postures.title: Transparency and System Documentation
postures.owner: MachineLearningStandards for model cards and limitations; AIStandards for system-level documentation

evidence.observation: Scope: 'Applies to every model whose output is used by anyone other than its author... The subject is a document that accompanies the model — a model card'.

postures.reasoning: ML 25 owns the model card outright. AIStandards documents the system around the model — its tools, its retrieval sources, its gates — for which no ML standard exists, and cites ML's template rather than copying it.

postures.title: User Disclosure of AI Involvement
postures.owner: AIStandards for whether disclosure is owed; UIUXDesignStandards for how it is presented

evidence.observation: Lede: 'This standard owns presentation; authorization, attribution, and auditability of AI actions belong to EngineeringStandards and are referenced rather than restated.' R1 requires generated content be marked where a user could take it for verified fact.

postures.reasoning: The plan marked this owned outright, which contradicts this pack's own Standard 7 R1 — that table already records UIUXDesignStandards as owner of how a disclosure is presented, with AIStandards owning only whether one is owed. The catalog posture was inconsistent with the standard; the standard is right and the posture is corrected.

postures.title: Operational Resilience, Degradation, and Provider Portability

evidence.observation: level required, severity error, validationType code-analysis, nonExemptible false. Description: 'Model providers sit behind an abstraction so capabilities remain stable when the model changes.'

postures.reasoning: Genuine precedent, and the plan's recommendation to claim it is upheld: provider lock-in is an operational-resilience concern and the brief names resilience. AIStandards mints cost.provider-portable; the ES rule stays in ES.

postures.title: Approval Gates for High-Impact, Destructive, and Irreversible Actions

evidence.observation: ai.destructive-approval is level required, nonExemptible true, with $exemptibilityNote: 'a project may declare this not-applicable when it has no destructive actions, but it may not waive approval while having them.'
R3: 'A user asked to approve MUST be able to see the change.' R2 governs the interface distinction between proposed and applied.

postures.reasoning: Two precedents, and they divide cleanly: ES owns the authorization model, UIUX owns what the approving user sees, AIStandards owns the classification of which model-initiated actions require a gate at all. The UIUX precedent was not in the plan's crosswalk table and is added.

notGovernedElsewhere.$comment: Items posture O after searching the nine packs for an owner and finding none. This is the negative control of the boundary review: an O recorded without a search is an assumption, not a posture.
searchedFor: grep over every pack's rules/*.json for the item's subject terms
the standards/ filename list of every pack

adjacenciesNotedButNotOwnership.note: UIUXDesignStandards has no prompt-security standard; EngineeringStandards 16 (Security) governs application security architecture, not prompt injection. No owner.

UIUXDesignStandards 19 (Performance as UX) and performance.budgets-testable govern perceived interface performance. Inference latency budgets are a different subject with no owner; the adjacency is recorded so a future reviewer does not rediscover it as a conflict.
No pack in the portfolio mentions environmental impact. This item's O posture is uncontested and its validation type is not-evaluable, so it will report as a stated requirement nothing checks.

sharedSegments.$comment: Rule id namespace segments AIStandards reserves that another pack also uses. Standard 7 R4 forbids a colliding FULL id, not a shared segment — but the approved plan claimed the seventeen segments were disjoint, and that claim is false. Declaring the overlap is the honest form; a shared segment is permitted, an undeclared one is a claim nobody checked.
sharedSegments.verifiedAgainst: all nine packs listed in packsRead, rule ids and aliases, on 2026-09-04

segments.note: Declared as an intentional overlap in the approved plan.

findings: The approved plan's claim that AIStandards' seventeen reserved namespace segments are disjoint from other packs' is false. Six are shared. No full rule id collides, verified across nine packs, so Standard 7 R4 holds — but the disjointness claim does not and has been replaced by an explicit declaration.

The foreign-namespace inventory covered four packs. Nine exist. It has been extended to all nine; the four-pack version could not have caught a collision with FinancialStandards' seven disclosure.* rules, and AIStandards reserves that segment.

Four postures changed on evidence: 25 X to O, 26 D to B, 27 O to B, 40 O to B. Two more were narrowed rather than changed: 18 and 30, where the named MachineLearningStandards standard covers half the concern and the plan deferred the whole of it.
The plan's B legend was ML-specific and could not express deference to UIUXDesignStandards or PredictionStandards. It has been generalised to name an owner per item.
Item 40's plan posture contradicted this pack's own Standard 7 R1 table. The standard was right; the catalog was wrong.
unresolved: No human has signed this review off. Every verdict here is this review's inference from an observed scope statement, and Standard 7 R1's evidence row requires human review that has not occurred.
None of the adjacent packs' maintainers has been asked to confirm any division recorded here. Every posture is unilateral, including the four that changed and the two that were narrowed.
This review is a snapshot at the recorded commits and has no staleness mechanism. A scope amended in any of the nine packs would silently invalidate a row.
